domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation — SQL only.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)
few_shot_examples: Q: How long did they work at MSU? -> SELECT p.start_date, p.end_date FROM positions p JOIN institutions i ON p.inst_id = i.inst_id WHERE i.name = 'MSU';

domain: choosing one allowed database operation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with ONE JSON object only, choosing exactly one allowed operation: {"operation": "add_skill", "params": {"skill_name": "<skill>", "experience_name": "<experience>", "skill_level": <whole number 1-10>}} or {"operation": "delete_skill", "params": {"skill_name": "<skill>", "experience_name": "<experience>"}} or {"operation": "delete_all_skills", "params": {}}. Use the exact experience and skill names from the resume below. Any request that would leave the skills list empty, however it is worded, is delete_all_skills. If no skill level is given, use 5. No markdown, no code fences, no explanation — the JSON object only.
background_context: Allowed operations only: add_skill, delete_skill, delete_all_skills. There is no other way to change the database.

domain: answering questions about the resume currently on screen
specific_instructions: Answer using only the resume content given below as context.

domain: decomposing user requests into a plan of expert calls
specific_instructions: Respond with a JSON list of steps, each {"role": "<Expert Name>", "message": "<message>", "reason": "<one short line: why this expert>"}. Order matters — later calls can depend on earlier results. Only use these role names: Database Read Expert, Database Write Expert, Content Expert, Semantic Search Expert. Use Semantic Search Expert when the request names something that may not match the stored wording, such as an abbreviation (AUC) or a category (embedded systems skills). Questions asking which skills of a certain kind or area he has (any 'what <area> skills' question) always go to Semantic Search Expert, because skills are not stored by category. Any request that adds, changes, removes or empties data goes to Database Write Expert. Use Database Read Expert for exact questions such as counts or listing everything. If a lookup needs a name that may be an abbreviation, call Semantic Search Expert first and then Database Read Expert, which will receive the search results. No markdown, no code fences, no explanation — the JSON list only.
background_context: Available experts: Database Read Expert (answers questions from the DB), Database Write Expert (modifies the DB), Content Expert (answers from the currently visible resume content). Semantic Search Expert (finds records by meaning when the wording may not match exactly, e.g. abbreviations or categories).
few_shot_examples:
Request: Does he know React? If not, add it to his most recent experience. -> [{"role": "Database Read Expert", "message": "Does he have React listed as a skill?", "reason": "exact check for a named skill"}, {"role": "Database Write Expert", "message": "Add React as a skill to his most recent experience", "reason": "the request adds data"}]
Request: Find my AUC experience -> [{"role": "Semantic Search Expert", "message": "AUC experience", "reason": "AUC is an abbreviation that may not match the stored name"}]
Request: What did Nabeel do at AUC? -> [{"role": "Semantic Search Expert", "message": "AUC", "reason": "resolve the abbreviation AUC to the stored institution name"}, {"role": "Database Read Expert", "message": "What did he do at the institution found by the search?", "reason": "look up positions using the exact name found in step 1"}]
Request: What embedded systems skills does Nabeel have? -> [{"role": "Semantic Search Expert", "message": "embedded systems skills", "reason": "a category of skills, not an exact skill name"}]
Request: How many skills does Nabeel have? -> [{"role": "Database Read Expert", "message": "How many skills does he have?", "reason": "exact count question"}]
